72_marg1134: Paul, a prisoner. He does not say “apostle,” a name of dignity, but of humility, because he does not command but entreats. As if to say: he whom you ought to pity should not be the cause of sorrow, if you, merciless, should torment the son?
72_marg1135: The Apostle does not say what is a name of dignity, but “prisoner,” which is a name of humility, because he does not command but entreats. For here there is an intercession for Onesimus. Therefore he recalls what belongs to humility, beginning from his own injury, that he might give dignity to his epistle. For as to be bound for the cause of sin is a disgrace, so on the other hand to endure the chains of custody for Christ is the greatest glory. For at that time he was in custody. Therefore he says: Paul, a prisoner, etc. As if to say: he whom you ought to have mercy on should not be the cause of grief; what will you be, if, merciless, you torment a son?

72_marg1141: The Apostle prays this: that his working be done with knowledge of goodness, that is, that he work with such a mind that he may thereafter expect a reward from it.
72_marg1142: Or thus. I am mindful of you and give thanks in my prayers held concerning this: that the communication of your faith, that is, the working of the faith by which you serve Christ and the saints, may be made evident in the acknowledgment of every good work that is in Christ Jesus, that is, with the knowledge of the eternal good, that it may be looked for as a reward. For the Apostle prays this, that his working may be done with the knowledge of goodness, that is, that he may work with such a mind that for the future he may look for Jesus Christ from it as reward, not the repayment of temporal things.
